newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan June jobless rate at 2.67 percent.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan June jobless rate at 2.67 percent.

text.p: Taiwan's unemployment rate was 2.67 percent in June, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Wednesday.

The June jobless figure came just slightly above an average 2.61 percent forecast compiled from a July 22 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists. The poll forecasts ranged from a low of 2.5 percent to a high of 2.73 percent.
The jobless rate in June exceeded the May rate of 2.51 percent, but was below the January-June average of 2.7 percent, the directorate noted.

Directorate official Chen Jin-cherng attributed the relatively high June rate mainly to a new crop of high school graduates' entering the job market, and saw the rate rising in July, a view shared by respondents the Reuters Poll.
"The unemployment level is expected to rise further in July and August as there will be more first-time job seekers -- mainly colleges and graduate schools graduates -- to look for jobs," Chen said.
Chen said the jobless rate for all of 1997 might exceed the government's latest target of 2.60 percent.

"Despite a recovering economy and continued growth in the services sector, the number of jobs being created are not enough to fully absorb the unemployed population who've lost jobs in labour-intensive industries," Chen said.
Chen gave no new estimate for 1997 joblessness.

Economists and officials had attributed the shift to higher joblessness to a fundamental economic change in Taiwan -- a move to service-oriented industries from the labour-intensive manufacturing that had engendered the island's dramatic economic development.

Taiwan's jobless rate held close to 1.5 percent in 1991-1994 but rose to 1.79 percent in 1995 and pushed above 3.0 percent in August, September and October 1996 -- a startling development on an island accustomed to rapid growth and brisk job creation.
The jobless rate was 2.60 percent for all of 1996.
The number of unemployed people in June increased 15,000 to 251,000 from May, while the number of employed decreased 7,000 to 9.131 million, the directorate said.
The average period of unemployment was 22 weeks, unchanged from May, it said.
